entries.rule: Score participant actions in Differential Reinforcement of Alternative Behavior (DRA), using the same rules for the video simulator and live simulated-learner sessions.

Teach 3 seconds for instructions, earned dolphin delivery, completed worksheet removal, and worksheet transitions; 10 seconds for waiting periods; 15 seconds for dolphin access. Scoring tolerances are not participant instructions.
For required actions, record occurrence separately from timing. Preserve event timestamps. A late action is delivered with a timing omission; do not also record it as entirely omitted.
A required action is never performed before its opportunity ends, after the complete response window elapsed. Timing is N/A.
A required action is performed after its scoring deadline.
An inappropriate action occurs: excess prompts, prompts during ongoing work, unearned dolphin delivery, or statements directing the learner to stop tapping or banging.

A scored action occurs too early: worksheet presentation, initial instruction, required prompt, worksheet removal, or dolphin removal. For an early required prompt or worksheet removal, occurrence is correct and timing is incorrect.

N/A means no applicable opportunity arose. Interrupted means an applicable opportunity arose but session cutoff prevented the full response window, with no action performed. Exclude both from scoring denominators.
All accepted windows include their endpoints: 0–3, 8–12, and 13–17 seconds.

Score opportunities actually reached. A complete correctly implemented catalog session plans 10 worksheet presentations, 10 initial instructions, 13 prompts, 5 earned deliveries, 10 worksheet removals, 5 dolphin removals, 4 tapping trials, and 4 banging trials. No unearned delivery and no excess prompts are scored once per trial; ongoing-work prompting is scored per applicable trial. Errors and cutoff may alter actual opportunities.
Assign worksheet presentation to the trial being introduced. Retain the scenario ID and fixed catalog trial position for every coded trial.
Coders must be able to review the relevant preceding event as well as the current trial. Record correct actions, errors, N/A, and Interrupted; preserve timestamps when actions occur.
Provide one worksheet at a time. Present trial 1 within 3 seconds of session start. For trials 2–10, present within 3 seconds of dolphin removal or removal of the preceding unfinished worksheet.

Identify trial number and reference event; record its time, worksheet presentation time, and session endpoint. Presentation is when the worksheet is placed in front of the learner and available to work on.
Presented within the applicable 3-second window. Record Presented: Yes; Timing: Correct.
entries.example: Dolphin removed at 2:00; worksheet presented at 2:02.

entries.rule: Presented before session start or before the preceding trial ends. Record Presented: Yes; Timing: Timing commission.
entries.example: Next worksheet provided while dolphin access continues.

entries.rule: Presented more than 3 seconds after the reference event. Record Presented: Yes; Timing: Timing omission.
entries.example: Dolphin removed at 2:00; worksheet presented at 2:05.

entries.rule: A worksheet is required, the full window elapsed, and it is never presented before session end. Record Presented: No; Occurrence: Omission; Timing: N/A.
entries.example: Dolphin removed at 9:55; no worksheet before session ends at 10:00.

entries.rule: A worksheet is required, but session cutoff occurs before its full 3-second window elapsed, without presentation.
entries.example: Dolphin removed at 9:59; no worksheet before cutoff at 10:00.

entries.rule: No further presentation opportunity arises because 10 trials are complete or the session has already ended.
entries.example: No trial 11 is required.

entries.rule: If presentation occurs before cutoff, retain its score even if the full window has not elapsed.
Give a clear direction to begin math work within 3 seconds of worksheet presentation. The first task direction after presentation is the initial instruction.
Exact words are not required in person. The direction must clearly tell the learner to begin the task.
entries.example: Start working. Do your math. Begin your worksheet. Complete two problems.

entries.rule: Record worksheet presentation and speech onset of the first subsequent task direction. In the simulator, use the task-direction button-press time.
Instruction begins within 3 seconds. Record Delivered: Yes; Timing: Correct.
entries.example: Direction begins 2 seconds after presentation.

entries.rule: Instruction begins more than 3 seconds later. Record Delivered: Yes; Timing: Timing omission.
entries.example: Direction begins 5 seconds after presentation.

entries.rule: No initial instruction before worksheet removal or session end, after the complete response window elapsed. Record Delivered: No; Occurrence: Omission; Timing: N/A.
A task direction occurs before presentation. Record separately; it does not satisfy the instruction required after presentation.
entries.example: Direction before presentation, followed by an on-time instruction: record the early error and the later correct action.

entries.rule: Session ends before the complete 3-second window elapsed, without an instruction.
entries.example: Worksheet at 9:59; no instruction before cutoff.

entries.rule: No worksheet is presented, so no post-presentation instruction opportunity arises.
The instruction is still required even when the learner starts immediately. Subsequent task directions count as prompts.
When the learner has not begun working, prompt after 10 seconds, measured from the initial instruction.
Any clear direction to begin or continue math work is acceptable in person. Later task directions are prompts regardless of exact wording.
entries.example: Do your math. Keep working. Finish your problems. Do the next problem.

entries.rule: Record the initial instruction, work onset or resumption, and speech onset of the prompt. Check the number of prompts already delivered.
Delivered 8–12 seconds after the initial instruction, while the stated condition still applies. Record Delivered: Yes; Timing: Correct.
entries.example: Instruction at 0:02; prompt at 0:12: on time.

entries.rule: A required prompt delivered before 8 seconds: occurrence correct; timing incorrect. Both measures enter the overall score. It counts toward the two-prompt maximum and triggers the scripted response.
A prompt during ongoing work or after two prompts is a commission under the applicable per-trial behavior measure, not a correctly delivered required prompt. Record every instance.
A required prompt is delivered after 12 seconds, while still applicable. Record Delivered: Yes; Timing: Timing omission.
A required prompt is never delivered before its opportunity ends, after the complete response window elapsed. Record Delivered: No; Occurrence: Omission; Timing: N/A.
Session cutoff occurs before the full prompt window elapsed, with no prompt delivered.
entries.example: Wait begins at 9:55; no prompt before cutoff at 10:00.

entries.rule: Premature worksheet removal ends a still-open prompt window with no prompt delivered: mark Terminated by participant and exclude. Preserve any omission already established before removal.
The learner begins or resumes work before a prompt is required, or this prompt opportunity never arises. Retain any inappropriate prompt actually delivered.
Do not create an extra omission for the same prompt merely because its delivered timing was incorrect. Preserve delivered, early, late, excess, and never-delivered distinctions.

entries.section: Second Prompt Following No Work Scoring
entries.rule: When work has not begun after the first prompt, prompt after 10 seconds, measured from the first prompt.

entries.section: Second Prompt Following No Work Scoring
entries.rule: Any clear direction to begin or continue math work is acceptable in person. Later task directions are prompts regardless of exact wording.
entries.example: Do your math. Keep working. Finish your problems. Do the next problem.

entries.section: Second Prompt Following No Work Scoring
entries.rule: Record the first prompt, work onset or resumption, and speech onset of the prompt. Check the number of prompts already delivered.

entries.section: Second Prompt Following No Work Scoring
entries.rule: Delivered 8–12 seconds after the first prompt, while the stated condition still applies. Record Delivered: Yes; Timing: Correct.
entries.example: First prompt at 0:12; second prompt at 0:22: on time.

entries.section: Second Prompt Following No Work Scoring
entries.rule: A required prompt delivered before 8 seconds: occurrence correct; timing incorrect. Both measures enter the overall score. It counts toward the two-prompt maximum and triggers the scripted response.

entries.section: Second Prompt Following No Work Scoring
entries.rule: A prompt during ongoing work or after two prompts is a commission under the applicable per-trial behavior measure, not a correctly delivered required prompt. Record every instance.

entries.section: Second Prompt Following No Work Scoring
entries.rule: A required prompt is delivered after 12 seconds, while still applicable. Record Delivered: Yes; Timing: Timing omission.

entries.section: Second Prompt Following No Work Scoring
entries.rule: A required prompt is never delivered before its opportunity ends, after the complete response window elapsed. Record Delivered: No; Occurrence: Omission; Timing: N/A.

entries.section: Second Prompt Following No Work Scoring
entries.rule: Session cutoff occurs before the full prompt window elapsed, with no prompt delivered.
entries.example: Wait begins at 9:55; no prompt before cutoff at 10:00.

entries.section: Second Prompt Following No Work Scoring
entries.rule: Premature worksheet removal ends a still-open prompt window with no prompt delivered: mark Terminated by participant and exclude. Preserve any omission already established before removal.

entries.section: Second Prompt Following No Work Scoring
entries.rule: The learner begins or resumes work before a prompt is required, or this prompt opportunity never arises. Retain any inappropriate prompt actually delivered.

entries.section: Second Prompt Following No Work Scoring
entries.rule: Do not create an extra omission for the same prompt merely because its delivered timing was incorrect. Preserve delivered, early, late, excess, and never-delivered distinctions.

entries.section: Prompt After One Completed Problem Scoring
entries.rule: When the second problem has not begun and a prompt remains available, prompt after 10 seconds, measured from completion of the first problem.

entries.section: Prompt After One Completed Problem Scoring
entries.rule: Any clear direction to begin or continue math work is acceptable in person. Later task directions are prompts regardless of exact wording.
entries.example: Do your math. Keep working. Finish your problems. Do the next problem.

entries.section: Prompt After One Completed Problem Scoring
entries.rule: Record completion of the first problem, work onset or resumption, and speech onset of the prompt. Check the number of prompts already delivered.

entries.section: Prompt After One Completed Problem Scoring
entries.rule: Delivered 8–12 seconds after completion of the first problem, while the stated condition still applies. Record Delivered: Yes; Timing: Correct.
entries.example: First problem completed at 0:20; prompt at 0:30: on time.

entries.section: Prompt After One Completed Problem Scoring
entries.rule: A required prompt delivered before 8 seconds: occurrence correct; timing incorrect. Both measures enter the overall score. It counts toward the two-prompt maximum and triggers the scripted response.

entries.section: Prompt After One Completed Problem Scoring
entries.rule: A prompt during ongoing work or after two prompts is a commission under the applicable per-trial behavior measure, not a correctly delivered required prompt. Record every instance.

entries.section: Prompt After One Completed Problem Scoring
entries.rule: A required prompt is delivered after 12 seconds, while still applicable. Record Delivered: Yes; Timing: Timing omission.

entries.section: Prompt After One Completed Problem Scoring
entries.rule: A required prompt is never delivered before its opportunity ends, after the complete response window elapsed. Record Delivered: No; Occurrence: Omission; Timing: N/A.

entries.section: Prompt After One Completed Problem Scoring
entries.rule: Session cutoff occurs before the full prompt window elapsed, with no prompt delivered.
entries.example: Wait begins at 9:55; no prompt before cutoff at 10:00.

entries.section: Prompt After One Completed Problem Scoring
entries.rule: Premature worksheet removal ends a still-open prompt window with no prompt delivered: mark Terminated by participant and exclude. Preserve any omission already established before removal.

entries.section: Prompt After One Completed Problem Scoring
entries.rule: The learner begins or resumes work before a prompt is required, or this prompt opportunity never arises. Retain any inappropriate prompt actually delivered.

entries.section: Prompt After One Completed Problem Scoring
entries.rule: Do not create an extra omission for the same prompt merely because its delivered timing was incorrect. Preserve delivered, early, late, excess, and never-delivered distinctions.

entries.section: Task Direction Classification and Prompt Limit
entries.rule: The first task direction after worksheet presentation is the initial instruction. All subsequent directions to begin or continue work are prompts, even if wording is identical.

entries.section: Task Direction Classification and Prompt Limit
entries.rule: Use one button: Say - Do your math work. Classify its presses by sequence, not label.

entries.section: Task Direction Classification and Prompt Limit
entries.rule: Allow two prompts per worksheet/trial, excluding the initial instruction. Every delivered prompt counts; the count does not reset after problem 1.

entries.section: Task Direction Classification and Prompt Limit
entries.rule: Early required prompt: timing commission. Prompt during ongoing work: commission. Third or later prompt: excess-prompt commission. Keep these classifications separate.

entries.section: Task Direction Classification and Prompt Limit
entries.rule: One early prompt plus one on-time prompt uses both prompts. Any further prompt is excessive.

entries.section: Task Direction Classification and Prompt Limit
entries.rule: When no instruction has been given, worksheet presentation provides the waiting-time reference. However, the first subsequent task direction still counts as the initial instruction, not as a prompt.

entries.section: Task Direction Classification and Prompt Limit
entries.rule: Immediate-start scenarios begin at worksheet presentation. Prompt-dependent scenarios respond to actual prompts, even if early; the initial instruction does not trigger their prompted response.

entries.section: Task Direction Classification and Prompt Limit
entries.rule: Keep a running count of task directions and prompts for each worksheet. Reset for the next worksheet. Do not assign initial-instruction status repeatedly to the same wording.
After the second prompt, wait 10 seconds without work, then remove the unfinished worksheet. Do not give the dolphin.
Record second-prompt onset, any subsequent work, and worksheet removal. Verify that two prompts were delivered and that work did not begin or resume during the final wait.
Removal 8–12 seconds after the second prompt while the learner remains inactive. Record Removed: Yes; Timing: Correct.
entries.example: Second prompt at 0:22; no work; removal at 0:32.

entries.rule: Worksheet removed before the allowed endpoint, including before two prompts or while work is ongoing. Record Removed: Yes / occurrence correct; timing incorrect.
Removal after 12 seconds while the requirement remains applicable. Record Removed: Yes; Timing: Timing omission.
Removal is required, the full window elapsed, and the worksheet is never removed before session end. Record Removed: No; Occurrence: Omission; Timing: N/A.
Session ends before the full removal window elapsed and no removal occurred.
This removal opportunity never arises, or work resumes during the final wait. If work subsequently stops after problem 1, use the next section.

Keep the worksheet available if work begins during the final wait. Removal while a problem is in progress is a premature-removal timing commission even if the preceding prompt clock reached 10 seconds.

entries.section: One Problem Completed After Both Prompts: Removal Scoring
entries.rule: Allow resumed work to continue. If problem 1 is completed after both prompts and the learner does not start problem 2, wait 10 seconds from completion of problem 1, then remove the worksheet. No third prompt.

entries.section: One Problem Completed After Both Prompts: Removal Scoring
entries.rule: Verify both prompts were used. Record first-problem completion, whether problem 2 begins, and removal time.

entries.section: One Problem Completed After Both Prompts: Removal Scoring
entries.rule: Removal at 8–12 seconds after first-problem completion, if problem 2 has not begun.
entries.example: Problem 1 completed at 0:35; no second-problem work; removal at 0:45.

entries.section: One Problem Completed After Both Prompts: Removal Scoring
entries.rule: Premature worksheet removal or removal during work: occurrence correct; timing incorrect. A third prompt is a separate excess-prompt commission.

entries.section: One Problem Completed After Both Prompts: Removal Scoring
entries.rule: Removal after 12 seconds while still required.

entries.section: One Problem Completed After Both Prompts: Removal Scoring
entries.rule: Required removal never occurs after the full response window elapsed. Timing is N/A.

entries.section: One Problem Completed After Both Prompts: Removal Scoring
entries.rule: Session cutoff prevents the full removal window, and no removal occurs.

entries.section: One Problem Completed After Both Prompts: Removal Scoring
entries.rule: This sequence does not occur, or problem 2 begins before removal is required.
Remove the worksheet within 3 seconds of completion of the second problem. Worksheet removal and dolphin delivery may occur in either order, but each must meet its own deadline.
Record second-problem completion and when the worksheet is removed. Score independently of the other action.
Action occurs within 3 seconds, including exactly 3 seconds. Record Occurred: Yes; Timing: Correct.
Action occurs more than 3 seconds after completion. Record Occurred: Yes; Timing: Timing omission.
entries.example: Second problem completed at 1:00; action at 1:05: late.

entries.rule: Action never occurs before its opportunity ends, after the full response window elapsed. Record Occurred: No; Occurrence: Omission; Timing: N/A.
Session ends before the full 3-second window elapsed, with no action.
entries.example: Second problem completed at 9:59; no action before 10:00.

entries.rule: Two problems are not completed, so this earned-action opportunity does not arise. Score any inappropriate action under the relevant commission rule.
An action that occurs before cutoff retains its score, even if the complete window has not elapsed.
Give the dolphin within 3 seconds of completion of the second problem. Worksheet removal and dolphin delivery may occur in either order, but each must meet its own deadline.
Record second-problem completion and when the dolphin becomes available to the learner. Score independently of the other action.
Action occurs within 3 seconds, including exactly 3 seconds. Record Occurred: Yes; Timing: Correct.
Action occurs more than 3 seconds after completion. Record Occurred: Yes; Timing: Timing omission.
entries.example: Second problem completed at 1:00; action at 1:05: late.

entries.rule: Action never occurs before its opportunity ends, after the full response window elapsed. Record Occurred: No; Occurrence: Omission; Timing: N/A.
Session ends before the full 3-second window elapsed, with no action.
entries.example: Second problem completed at 9:59; no action before 10:00.

entries.rule: Two problems are not completed, so this earned-action opportunity does not arise. Score any inappropriate action under the relevant commission rule.
An action that occurs before cutoff retains its score, even if the complete window has not elapsed.

Score worksheet-removal occurrence and timing once per trial. Use the completed-work or unfinished-work reference as applicable. Do not add a second removal component solely because both branches are described in this appendix.
Even when no valid removal deadline has yet arisen, an actual premature removal receives occurrence correct and timing commission. Do not mark that actual removal N/A.
Premature removal also ends unfinished instruction/prompt windows. Mark those windows Terminated by participant if their deadlines have not elapsed; preserve omissions already established.
Withhold the dolphin until two problems are completed. Tapping or banging does not alter this requirement.
Review dolphin deliveries throughout the trial and determine how many problems had been completed at each delivery.

Score no unearned delivery once in every trial, including trials eventually completing two problems. No delivery before two problems is correct. For partial trials, require at least 3 seconds with fewer than two problems complete.
entries.example: One problem completed; worksheet eventually removed; no dolphin given: correct withholding.

entries.rule: Dolphin delivered before two problems are complete. Record each observed delivery with its timestamp.
entries.example: Dolphin given while Sam bangs and has completed zero problems.

entries.rule: Count correct withholding when fewer than two problems were complete for at least 3 seconds and no unearned delivery occurred. Retain any actual unearned delivery regardless of duration. Shorter incomplete observations without delivery are excluded.
Dolphin delivered after one problem, then problem 2 is completed: unearned-delivery commission. Later completion does not erase it.
Dolphin delivered only after two problems: no-unearned-delivery score correct. Score earned-delivery occurrence and timing separately.
Dolphin delivered before work or during tapping/banging with fewer than two completed problems: unearned-delivery commission.
Once two problems are completed, use Earned Dolphin Delivery Scoring. Do not treat earned delivery during tapping or banging as a commission.
After earned dolphin delivery, allow 15 seconds of access, then remove the dolphin.

For earned delivery only, judge whether removal occurred and whether access lasted 13–17 seconds. Score occurrence and timing separately; do not add a duplicate duration score. Exact timestamp entry is not required.
Removal at 13–17 seconds of access, inclusive. Record Removed: Yes; Timing: Correct.
Removal before 13 seconds. Record Removed: Yes; Timing: Timing commission.
entries.example: Dolphin removed after 10 seconds.

entries.rule: Removal after 17 seconds. Record Removed: Yes; Timing: Timing omission.
entries.example: Dolphin removed after 20 seconds.

entries.rule: Dolphin never removed before session end after the full 17-second window elapsed. Record Removed: No; Occurrence: Omission; Timing: N/A.
Session ends before the full 17-second window elapsed, without removal.
entries.example: Access begins at 9:50; no removal before 10:00.

entries.rule: No earned dolphin delivery occurred, including trials with only inappropriate delivery. Exclude both removal occurrence and duration/timing.
Do not score removal or access duration for inappropriate delivery. Record the inappropriate-delivery commission; removal occurrence and timing are N/A.
If the dolphin is removed before cutoff, retain the score, even if the window would otherwise have been interrupted.
entries.example: Removal at 10 seconds of access followed by session end: timing commission remains.

entries.rule: Continue the procedure without commenting on finger tapping or changing the task requirement. Give the dolphin after two completed problems; otherwise withhold it.
Identify whether finger tapping occurred and record any direction to stop it. Review worksheet and dolphin actions under their respective scoring sections.
No direction to stop finger tapping during a completed applicable trial, or during a partial trial with at least 3 seconds of observable finger tapping.
Say Please stop tapping the table, or an equivalent statement directing the learner to stop the behavior. Record the statement onset.
No finger tapping observation opportunity arises. An inappropriate stop statement actually delivered is still retained as a commission event.

Retain any actual stop statement regardless of exposure duration. Without a stop statement, include a partial trial as correct only after at least 3 seconds of observable behavior; shorter observations are excluded.
Behavior visible for 4 seconds before early trial termination; no stop statement: correct no-comment score. Behavior visible for 1 second and participant says Stop: commission.
Premature worksheet removal receives a timing commission; unearned dolphin delivery receives a commission. Do not infer causation from timing alone.
Continue the procedure without commenting on table banging or changing the task requirement. Give the dolphin after two completed problems; otherwise withhold it.
Identify whether table banging occurred and record any direction to stop it. Review worksheet and dolphin actions under their respective scoring sections.
No direction to stop table banging during a completed applicable trial, or during a partial trial with at least 3 seconds of observable table banging.
Say Please stop banging the table, or an equivalent statement directing the learner to stop the behavior. Record the statement onset.
No table banging observation opportunity arises. An inappropriate stop statement actually delivered is still retained as a commission event.

Retain any actual stop statement regardless of exposure duration. Without a stop statement, include a partial trial as correct only after at least 3 seconds of observable behavior; shorter observations are excluded.
Behavior visible for 4 seconds before early trial termination; no stop statement: correct no-comment score. Behavior visible for 1 second and participant says Stop: commission.
Premature worksheet removal receives a timing commission; unearned dolphin delivery receives a commission. Do not infer causation from timing alone.
Two independent unlabeled timers may be used for reminders, waits, or dolphin access. The separate visible session clock runs automatically.
Record timer use if observed. It is separate from procedural scoring.
Not using a timer is not an omission or commission. Correctness depends on the actions and timing, not timer operation.
End after 10 trials or at 10 minutes. There is no one-minute maximum per trial.
Any action before cutoff retains its score, including early, late, and inappropriate actions.
If the response deadline has not been reached at cutoff and no action occurred, mark Interrupted and exclude from the denominator.
If the complete response window elapsed before cutoff and no action occurred, retain the omission score.
If the triggering event never occurred before session end, mark N/A rather than Interrupted.
Dolphin removed after 10 seconds of access and session then ends: retain timing commission.
Session ends at 10 seconds of access without removal: Interrupted.
Dolphin access exceeds 17 seconds and no removal occurs before cutoff: omission; timing N/A.
A participant prematurely removes the worksheet. Score removal occurrence as correct and removal timing as a timing commission.
If no instruction or prompt was delivered and its response deadline had not elapsed, mark Terminated by participant and exclude the unfinished window from scoring.
If no action was delivered and the full deadline elapsed before removal, retain its omission score.
Keep occurrence and timing scores for actions already performed, including early actions.
Worksheet at 0:00; removed at 0:01 without instruction: removal timing commission; instruction window Terminated by participant.
Worksheet at 0:00; removed at 0:05 without instruction: removal timing commission; instruction omission retained.
Use the separate 3-second exposure rules for correct withholding and no-comment scores. Actual commissions always remain in the record.
Correct if no third prompt occurs. Incorrect as a commission if one or more third/later prompts occur. Exclude the initial instruction from the prompt count.
Record every excess prompt and its timestamp, but give only one incorrect no-excess-prompts score per trial.
Initial instruction plus two prompts: correct. Initial instruction plus three prompts: incorrect. Five prompts still produce one incorrect trial score, with three excess events logged.
An early prompt still uses one of the two prompts; it cannot be ignored to allow an additional prompt.

entries.section: No Prompts During Ongoing Work Scoring
entries.rule: Correct if no prompt occurs while an individual problem is in progress. Incorrect as a commission if any do. The required initial instruction remains separate even if immediate work has begun.

entries.section: No Prompts During Ongoing Work Scoring
entries.rule: If no individual problem begins, no ongoing-work observation opportunity arises. Retain any actual commission and record only applicable behavior scores.

entries.section: No Prompts During Ongoing Work Scoring
entries.rule: Record each prompt during ongoing work. Every delivered prompt counts toward the two-prompt limit.

entries.section: No Prompts During Ongoing Work Scoring
entries.rule: Learner inactive; required prompt given at 5 seconds: occurrence correct, timing commission.

entries.section: No Prompts During Ongoing Work Scoring
entries.rule: Learner writing an answer; participant says Keep working: ongoing-work commission.

entries.section: No Prompts During Ongoing Work Scoring
entries.rule: A third prompt delivered while writing violates both no-excess-prompts and no-prompts-during-work measures. Score each measure separately; retain one event with both classifications.

entries.section: Overall Session Score and Individual Summaries
entries.rule: Overall procedural fidelity (%) = number of correct applicable scores divided by total applicable scores, multiplied by 100. Use this percentage for the session-by-session graph.

entries.section: Overall Session Score and Individual Summaries
entries.rule: Required-action occurrence and timing each contribute separately. Include applicable per-trial behavior measures, including no unearned delivery, no excess prompts, no prompts during work, and no stop statements for each relevant behavior.

entries.section: Overall Session Score and Individual Summaries
entries.rule: Occurrence correct; timing correct: 2 correct scores out of 2 applicable scores.

entries.section: Overall Session Score and Individual Summaries
entries.rule: Occurrence correct; timing omission: 1 correct score out of 2 applicable scores.

entries.section: Overall Session Score and Individual Summaries
entries.rule: For an early required prompt or worksheet removal: occurrence correct; timing commission: 1 correct score out of 2 applicable scores.

entries.section: Overall Session Score and Individual Summaries
entries.rule: Occurrence omission; timing N/A: 0 correct scores out of 1 applicable score. Do not add an incorrect timing score for an omitted action.

entries.section: Overall Session Score and Individual Summaries
entries.rule: Exclude N/A, Interrupted, and Terminated by participant entries from the applicable-score denominator. Retain applicable scores and all actual commission events.

entries.section: Overall Session Score and Individual Summaries
entries.rule: The denominator may vary because timing is N/A for omitted actions and some opportunities are not reached or are terminated. Report correct-score count and applicable-score count with the percentage.

entries.section: Overall Session Score and Individual Summaries
entries.rule: Report each component’s occurrence and timing separately, along with commission, omission, timing commission, and timing omission classifications. Preserve raw event counts as well as per-trial scores.

entries.section: Overall Session Score and Individual Summaries
entries.rule: A late instruction contributes 1/2, an on-time prompt 2/2, an omitted earned delivery 0/1, and correct no-unearned-delivery 1/1. Combined: 4 correct / 6 applicable = 66.7%. These are illustrative scores, not a complete session.

entries.section: Math Work: Beginning, Completion, and Pauses
entries.rule: An individual problem begins with the first writing movement directed at solving it. Use this marker for video tags and live coding.

entries.section: Math Work: Beginning, Completion, and Pauses
entries.rule: An individual problem is completed when its written answer is finished. Do not use the end of the video clip as a substitute.

entries.section: Math Work: Beginning, Completion, and Pauses
entries.rule: Once a problem starts, treat it as ongoing work until its answer is finished, including brief pauses. The simulated learner always finishes a problem they begin.

entries.section: Math Work: Beginning, Completion, and Pauses
entries.rule: After problem 1 is completed, the next 10-second wait applies only if problem 2 has not begun.

entries.section: Math Work: Beginning, Completion, and Pauses
entries.rule: Record problem 1 and problem 2 start/completion timestamps using the same definitions. Do not code a brief within-problem pause as a new prompt opportunity.

entries.section: Video Simulator: Recording and Automatic Scoring
entries.rule: Record participant ID, session ID, date/time, catalog version, set ID, and exact fixed order. Select one of the 324 catalog entries and never reshuffle its stored order.

entries.section: Video Simulator: Recording and Automatic Scoring
entries.rule: Record trial position, scenario ID, behavior condition, and planned work/prompt pattern.

entries.section: Video Simulator: Recording and Automatic Scoring
entries.rule: Timestamp worksheet presentation/removal, task directions, dolphin delivery/removal, stop statements, and timer operations.

entries.section: Video Simulator: Recording and Automatic Scoring
entries.rule: Tag actual video playback points for the start and completion of each problem. Record events only when playback reaches them.

entries.section: Video Simulator: Recording and Automatic Scoring
entries.rule: Apply the shared rules to actual events. Preserve raw timestamps, occurrence, elapsed time, timing/error categories, and reasons for N/A or Interrupted.

entries.section: Video Simulator: Recording and Automatic Scoring
entries.rule: Instruction timing uses button press. Physical-action and access timing must correspond to when the action or availability change is actually represented in playback, so video transitions do not distort the measure.

entries.section: Video Simulator: Recording and Automatic Scoring
entries.rule: Provide event log, trial scores, and session summary with catalog version, set ID, and observed sequence.
Record participant ID, session ID, date/time, catalog version, set ID, fixed planned order, observer ID, and primary/secondary role.
Coders must be able to identify the previous trial endpoint and current worksheet introduction. Assign presentation scores to the incoming trial.
Record session start/end, worksheet events, speech onset of task directions and stop statements, problem starts/completions, dolphin access/removal, and timer use.
Provide explicit correct/error choices and occurrence/timing fields for each component. Include component-specific N/A and Interrupted guidance rather than generic buttons without definitions.
Calculate elapsed times from coded event timestamps to assist score entry and flag inconsistencies for review. Preserve the coder’s observation and any corrections.
Record actual events, including departures from the selected scenario. Do not fill in actions merely because the script called for them.
Provide notes for script deviations, obscured events, and unreliable timestamps. Flag uncertain events for review rather than assuming a score.
Export event log, trial scores, and session summary with observer identity, catalog version, set ID, and actual sequence.
